qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: US macro tower network embeds non-cancellable 5-15 year master leases with ~3% annual contractual escalators and ~90% incremental colocation margins. However, overall corporate capital efficiency was diluted to sub-6% ROIC by a disastrous $19B+ fiber and small-cell rollup.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 5 (Score = 0, REJECT). While pure-play US macro towers are irreplaceable physical infrastructure with contractual ~3% escalators, executive leadership pursued a decade-long value-destructive M&A rollup in fiber/small cells ($19B+ spent at sub-hurdle returns). This empire-building resulted in ballooning debt (~$22B+), severe shareholder dilution, an activist proxy battle, three CEO changes in two years, an $8.5B fiber asset fire-sale at a steep realized loss, and a ~32% dividend cut. Flunks Munger/Thorndike capital allocation standard.
qualitative.evidence: Historical 10-year GAAP ROIC averaged just 5.9%, far below the 12% hurdle, driven by capital-intensive fiber rollups. Total debt peaked above $22B with interest coverage of ~2.5x-3.0x, far below the 5.0x fortress threshold. Following intense activist pressure from Elliott Management, former CEO Jay Brown departed in Jan 2024; Crown Castle agreed in 2024-2025 to sell its fiber and small cell business for $8.5B to Zayo/EQT to pay down >$7B of debt, and slashed the dividend by ~32% from $6.26 to $4.25 per share.
